lessons.title: A name for a number
lessons.explanation: A variable gives a value a name. In Python, apples = 3 stores the number 3 using the name apples.
lessons.question: After apples = 3, what value does apples hold?
hints: Look at the number on the right side of the equals sign.
lessons.success: Yes! apples now holds the number 3.

lessons.title: Use your variable
lessons.explanation: Python can calculate using a variable. If apples = 3, then apples + 1 is 4.
lessons.question: If stars = 5, what is stars + 2?
lessons.success: Exactly: 5 + 2 = 7. You used a variable in a calculation!

lessons.title: Sharing a pizza
lessons.explanation: A fraction describes equal parts of a whole. One half means one of two equal parts.
lessons.question: A pizza is cut into 4 equal pieces. You eat 2 pieces. How many pieces are left?
hints: Start with 4 pieces and take away 2.
lessons.success: Correct! Two pieces remain: half of the pizza.

lessons.title: Different pieces, same share
lessons.explanation: One half and two quarters describe the same amount. Cutting the pieces smaller does not change the amount of pizza.
lessons.question: Which fraction is equal to 1/2?
hints: Half of four pieces is two pieces.
lessons.success: Yes! 2/4 and 1/2 describe the same share.

title: My book report
subject: Writing
objectives: Support an opinion with an example

lessons.title: Tell me about your book
lessons.explanation: Write about a book you have read. Explain what happens, describe a character and give your opinion with an example. Your parent will read your report and help you revise it.
lessons.question: What should another reader know about this book?
rubric: Summarizes the main events in the writer's own words
Describes a character with an example
Supports an opinion with a detail from the book
Uses clear sentences and checks punctuation
hints: Start with the title and what the story is about.
lessons.success: Your parent has approved your report.

title: Python lab: variables and loops
subject: Python
objectives: Use a variable in a calculation
Use a loop to print a sequence

lessons.title: Count your stars
lessons.explanation: A variable names a value. Use stars = 5, then print the result of adding 2.
lessons.question: Write a program that stores 5 in a variable and prints 7 by adding 2.
hints: Use print(stars + 2) after assigning the variable.
lessons.success: Your variable program printed 7. Ready to try a loop!

lessons.title: Count with a loop
lessons.explanation: A for loop repeats its indented instructions. range(1, 6) produces the numbers 1 through 5.
lessons.question: Use a for loop to print 1 through 5, one number per line.
hints: Put print(number) inside the loop. Keep it indented.
lessons.success: Your loop printed all five numbers in order!
